title: Network waterfalls and request prioritization
description: Learn about Network waterfalls and request prioritization. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Network waterfalls and request prioritization are critical concepts for understanding and optimizing web performance. A network waterfall visualizes how resources load over time, while request prioritization ensures critical resources load first, reducing perceived load time.
Understanding Network Waterfalls

A network waterfall is a visualization of network requests over time, showing when each request starts, its duration, and dependencies between requests. Long waterfalls indicate sequential loading patterns that can be optimized.
Analyzing Waterfalls
Use browser DevTools Network tab to analyze waterfalls. Look for long chains of sequential requests, large gaps between requests, and resources that block critical rendering.

data.title: Common Waterfall Patterns
data.content: Identify performance issues in network waterfalls.
data.code:
Common waterfall patterns:

1. Sequential waterfall (bad):
   HTML → CSS → Font → JS → Image → Image → Image
   Each request waits for the previous one to complete.

2. Parallel waterfall (good):
   HTML → CSS, Font, JS (parallel) → Images (parallel)
   Multiple requests load simultaneously.

3. Mixed waterfall (common):
   HTML → CSS, JS (parallel) → API call → Render images
   Some parallel loading with strategic sequential dependencies.

data.text: Request Prioritization

Browsers prioritize requests automatically, but you can influence this priority. Critical resources like HTML, CSS, and fonts get high priority, while lower-priority resources like images and scripts get lower priority.

data.text: Resource Hints
Resource hints tell the browser about resources that will be needed soon, allowing it to optimize loading order and timing.

data.title: Resource Hints Usage
data.content: Use resource hints to optimize loading order.
data.code:
<!-- DNS resolution (earliest stage) -->
<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://cdn.example.com">

<!-- Preconnect (DNS + TCP + TLS) -->
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://api.example.com">

<!-- Prefetch (fetch resource for next navigation) -->
<link rel="prefetch" href="/next-page.js" as="script">

<!-- Preload (fetch resource for current page) -->
<link rel="preload" href="/critical.css" as="style">
<link rel="preload" href="/hero-font.woff2" as="font" crossorigin>

<!-- Prerender (load and render next page) -->
<link rel="prerender" href="/next-page">

data.text: Optimizing Request Chains
Reduce request chains by inlining critical CSS, using HTTP/2 multiplexing, and eliminating unnecessary redirects. Each redirect adds a round-trip to the waterfall.

data.title: Critical CSS Inlining
data.content: Inline critical CSS to eliminate render-blocking requests.
data.code:
<style>
  /* Critical CSS for above-fold content */
  body { font-family: system-ui; margin: 0; }
  .hero { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #667eea 0%, #764ba2 100%); }
  .hero-title { color: white; font-size: 2.5rem; }
</style>

<!-- Load the rest of CSS asynchronously -->
<link rel="preload" href="/styles.css" as="style" onload="this.onload=null;this.rel='stylesheet'">
<noscript><link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles.css"></noscript>

data.text: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 Benefits

HTTP/2 enables multiplexing, allowing multiple requests to be sent over a single connection simultaneously. HTTP/3 (QUIC) further improves performance with better congestion control and connection migration.

items: HTTP/2: Multiplexing, header compression, server push
HTTP/3: QUIC transport, better connection handling, improved security
Both eliminate the need for domain sharding
Enable server push for critical resources (with caution)

data.text: Connection Reuse
Reuse existing connections by keeping them alive (Keep-Alive) and using connection pooling. This reduces the overhead of establishing new connections for each request.

data.title: Connection Pooling in Node.js
data.content: Configure HTTP agent for connection reuse.

data.text: Avoiding Request Waterfalls

items: Inline critical CSS and font data URIs for above-fold content
Use HTTP/2 multiplexing instead of domain sharding
Preload critical resources that would otherwise waterfall
Implement early data hints for critical API calls
Consider service worker caching for repeated requests

data.title: Preload Carefully
data.text: Don't preload everything. Preloading uses bandwidth and can compete with critical resources. Only preload resources that are definitely needed and high-priority.
Monitoring Network Performance
Use Resource Timing API to measure network performance in production. Monitor waterfall patterns, request timings, and identify bottlenecks.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Network waterfalls reveal loading patterns and optimization opportunities
Long sequential waterfalls indicate performance issues
Use fetchpriority to influence browser request prioritization
Resource hints (preconnect, preload, prefetch) optimize loading order
Inline critical CSS to eliminate render-blocking requests
HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 enable parallel loading and better connection handling
Reuse connections and avoid unnecessary redirects
Monitor network performance with Resource Timing API
data.takeaway: Understanding and optimizing network waterfalls and request prioritization is essential for reducing load times and improving perceived performance.
